narrative:
The model predicts you have a 31% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to help you graduate.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this prediction were your reason for choosing the school, your lack of desire to pursue higher education, and your history of past failures. Choosing this school for its reputation actually worked in your favor and pushed the prediction toward passing. However, two powerful factors pulled strongly in the opposite direction. First, you have stated that you do not want to continue to higher education; among students who passed, every single one said they did want to continue studying, so this absence of ambition was a major red flag for the model. Second, you have already failed three classes in the past, while students who ultimately passed had zero previous failures on average. This track record of repeated setbacks was a very strong signal that you are at risk.

To improve, you should seriously reflect on why you no longer want to pursue further education and whether that view can change. At the same time, focus immediately on breaking the pattern of failure by attending every class, reducing your ten absences (more than double the average of students who passed), and using the extra support now being offered through remedial courses. Small, consistent changes in these areas can still shift your outcome.
